argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0209b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0209.

PROJECT
The team is designing a children's educational tablet case.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Laura  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Tomasz  ABSENT, never speaks
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Ben  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0209a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, the team introduced themselves, and she presented the project: a case for the company's existing Learnly seven-inch children's educational tablet. She gave the financial targets of a selling price of 25 Euros and a maximum production cost of 12.50 Euros per case, excluding packaging. The team agreed to keep the target age group of four to eight, and confirmed that the case only needs to fit the Learnly seven-inch tablet. In brainstorming, the industrial designer stressed drop protection using rubber or foam with thick corners. The team discussed a carrying handle, a handle that folds into a stand, bright colours that still appeal to parents, swappable covers, a screen flap versus a raised lip, easy cleaning, and a name tag window. The project manager then assigned the preparation tasks for the functional design meeting.
  decisions: The target group is children aged four to eight. The case only has to fit the company's Learnly seven-inch tablet; there is no universal fit. The case should be made of an easy-to-clean, wipeable material.
  actions: The marketing expert will research what parents and teachers want from the case, possibly with a short survey. The user interface designer will look at the functional side of the case, including the handle and access to the buttons and charging port. The industrial designer will research drop test standards and impact ratings. The user interface designer offered to do this first, but the industrial designer took it. The industrial designer will look into materials (rubber, foam, plastics) that fit the budget. The project manager will write up the minutes and send them round. Someone should check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases. Nobody took this task.
  problems: It is unclear whether the 25 Euro price is competitive, because no one knows what competing cases cost, and no one was assigned to find out. The 12.50 Euro cost limit may rule out features that add parts, such as swappable covers. Whether the handle should double as a stand is open. The user interface designer worried that a foldable stand could pinch children's fingers. The name tag window idea was parked without a decision. The wide four-to-eight age range covers users with quite different needs.
  action item SY0209a.ai1: Research what parents and teachers want from a children's tablet case, possibly via a short survey (owner B, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai2: Work out the functional side of the case: how children use it, the handle, and access to the buttons and charging port (owner C, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai3: Look into drop tests: the heights competing cases are rated for and the relevant impact standards (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai4: Investigate materials (rubber, foam, plastics) that fit the production budget (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai5: Write up the meeting minutes and send them to the team (owner A, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai6: Check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases (owner no owner, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a carrying handle; it was not decided.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested that the handle fold out into a stand; it was kept as an idea only, because of a finger-pinching concern.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested swappable colour covers; the industrial designer objected on cost.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested a screen flap; the user interface designer doubted it would survive young children, and the discussion moved to a raised lip around the screen.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a name tag window; it was parked without agreement.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_REASSIGNED_OR_DROPPED [F2]: A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F2]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
